parsed.draft_response:
Hi there—thanks for reaching out, and I’m sorry for the trouble here.

I understand your card was charged twice for the annual plan renewal on May 1, and the invoices involved are **INV-9031** and **INV-9032**. You’d like us to reverse one charge and confirm which invoice should remain in your accounting.

We’ll need our billing team to review these two charges to determine which one is the correct/duplicate transaction and what action to take. To help them confirm quickly, could you please share:
1) The **amount** charged on **INV-9031** and **INV-9032** (as shown on your invoice/statement)
2) The **account/email** on the subscription (or the last 4 digits of the card used)
3) Whether either charge is marked **pending** or **completed** (or if you’ve already received any partial refund)

Once we have that, we’ll proceed with the appropriate adjustment and follow up confirming which invoice should be kept for your records.

Thanks—this is marked high priority and is being escalated for human review.
promised_actions: Escalate to the billing team for human review of INV-9031 and INV-9032
Follow up after review with the appropriate billing adjustment
Confirm which invoice should remain in your accounting once verified
safety_notes: Do not promise a reversal/refund until billing team verifies the transactions
Do not confirm which invoice is valid without reviewing amounts, account identifier, and transaction status
Acknowledge urgency and escalation without claiming resolution

Customer requests confirmation of which invoice should remain in their accounting system.
